name: CLI command discovery — primary
description: Golden retrieval cases for the cli-health command corpus: strong intent->command matches, a known lexical-gap case, known-weak concept queries, and a gibberish junk-rejection case. Soft labels only (never a build gate). CALIBRATION (2026-06-04, run 164528ee): bands target the DEFAULT config — rerank ON via the cross-encoder (BAAI/bge-reranker-v2-m3) — whose scores are 0..1 relevance (strong matches ~0.85-1.0, junk ~0). NOTE: the provider's result id_field is `name` (the command's leaf token, e.g. `restart`, `logs`, `duplicates`), so expect_ids assert on leaf names, not full command paths; ambiguous leaves (e.g. `scenario`) are asserted by score+topk instead. If the cross-encoder resource is down the leg degrades to dense (cosine) order on a different scale and these bands will mislabel — check ConfigSnapshot.reranker_leg before trusting a run.

Asserted by score+topk, not id: the top hit's leaf (`scenario`) is too common to assert on. Cross-encoder ~0.86 for the validate command at #1.

file-tools files duplicates IS the #1 hit, but the cross-encoder honestly down-weights it (~0.2) because the command targets duplicate FILES while the query says CODE. Asserted by RANK only — deliberately NO score floor, since low confidence here is correct behavior, not a regression.

No dedicated 'remove bookmark' command exists; the cross-encoder returns the nearest action at ~0.01. Expectation is only that the query returns SOMETHING plausible (non-empty), not a confident match.
known weak — concept vs keyword; informational (no hard expectation)

Junk rejection under the rerank-on default: the cross-encoder scores this ~0.000. Ceiling tightened from the cosine-era 0.4 to 0.1 so any real leakage (or a dense-fallback run, which leaks ~0.58) is flagged.
